subject: Cloud islanding: on-prem scope, ops headcount & architecture clarifications
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@greenbank.com>, Aaron Perez <a.perez@edgecloud.io>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 10 Feb 2028 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: Cloud islanding: on-prem scope, ops headcount & architecture clarifications

Emily / Aaron —

Thanks for the detailed scope doc attached. To make this concrete for the internal feasibility and procurement path I need a short confirmation of a few items from you and the Greenbank security team so we can build an accurate mutual action plan: 

- Single-tenant VPC (no shared hardware): yes/no? If yes, do you require customer-owned VPC or is vendor-managed isolated VPC acceptable?
- Expected average QPS and 95th p50/p95 latency targets for conversational flows (tokens/sec or requests/min helps).
- Data residency and retention constraints (are there write-once logs, or do you require short-lived ephemeral KV caches only?).
- Required certifications: SOC2 + any additional controls (ISO, PCI scoping)? Which controls are must-haves vs. nice-to-have?
- KMS/HSM integration: do you have an HSM vendor preference and procurement timeline?

Attached: greenbank-scope-reqs.pdf (your doc) and initial-map.xlsx (our draft mutual action plan). If you can confirm the bullets above by EOD Monday we’ll produce an ops + headcount estimate and a pilot timeline.

Proposed immediate deliverables from Redwood:
- One-page architecture options (air-gapped on-prem VM vs. customer VPC vs. colocated isolated tenancy)
- Ops staffing model (SRE + infra oncall + infosec reviewer) for a 3-month pilot and for steady-state
- Risk ladder with gating criteria for go/no-go

I’ll schedule a 30 min sync next week to walk through the tradeoffs — suggested times in the MAP link.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Strategic GTM
Redwood Inference

Attachments: greenbank-scope-reqs.pdf, initial-map.xlsx
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Emily Chen <emily.chen@greenbank.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 13 Feb 2028 10:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Cloud islanding: on-prem scope, ops headcount & architecture clarifications

Vanessa / Emily —

Quick technical clarifications from the infra side to make the architecture options useful: 

1) Networking: if Greenbank wants vendor-managed isolated VPC, we need the following NAT/egress policy detail: will all egress to internet be blocked and routed through Greenbank egress proxies, or are selective outbound connections allowed for updates/metrics? If fully locked down we should plan an outbound whitelist tunnel and local relay.

2) Storage: are there restrictions on persistent KV cache lifetime? For throughput we normally rely on a local NVMe cache for tokenizer matrices — if persistence is blocked, we’ll need to size restart warm-up windows into the SLO.

3) Hardware & placement: do you have a preferred on-prem form factor (1U GPU host vs. 2U multi-socket) and networking fabric (25G/100G)? This affects rack count and power budgeting.

4) Ops SLA: what on-call window is Greenbank comfortable with for a pilot (4hr vs. 1hr response)? That drives headcount.

I’ve sketched three architecture candidates in arch-assumptions.md (attached) — low-touch vendor-managed isolated VPC, hybrid VPC with customer egress, and fully customer-hosted on-prem appliance. Key diffs: caching behavior, recovery windows, and quantization/latency tradeoffs.

If Emily can reply inline to the four bullets above we’ll convert the candidates into a sizing and runbook.

—Karthik
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: arch-assumptions.md

Subject: Re: Cloud islanding: on-prem scope, ops headcount & architecture clarifications

Vanessa / Karthik —

Thanks — quick answers inline. Apologies for brevity, procurement looped in for timeline.

- Single-tenant VPC: vendor-managed isolated VPC is acceptable for the pilot. For production we expect the option to move to customer-owned VPC.
- Egress policy: all outbound internet is blocked by default. We allow an approved whitelist for metrics/export only through our proxy.
- KV cache: allowed if the cache is ephemeral and keys are rotated every 24 hours; no persistent logs containing PII.
- Certifications: SOC2 Type II required. ISO 27001 preferred but not mandatory for pilot. PCI will be out of scope.
- KMS/HSM: Greenbank uses Thales HSM for primary key storage. Procurement indicates HSM onboarding takes ~10 weeks once legal is in place.

Procurement: our target for contractual review is EOM March; if we can lock a scope/pilot plan this month we’ll priority that review.

Emily Chen
Head of Cloud Security Programs
Greenbank Financial

Thanks Emily — that is exactly the clarity we needed. Next steps and internal asks below: 

1) Redwood deliverables by Feb 21:
   - Ops headcount estimate for pilot (we will provide 2 pilot options: 4hr and 1hr response SLAs)
   - One-page runbook for egress whitelisting and metrics relay to comply with your proxy requirements
   - Pilot architecture options doc mapped to your HSM timeline (we’ll propose a short-term pilot using envelope encryption and a roadmap to full Thales HSM integration)

2) Internal approvals required at Redwood: engineering commit for pilot SRE coverage, legal draft for SOC2 addendum, and product sign-off on model variant allowed in customer network. Kimberly / Marcus — please confirm availability for a 45 min internal alignment tomorrow afternoon so we can finalize the MAP for procurement.

3) Procurement path: Emily, you mentioned an EOM March target for contract review. We’ll attach the pilot MAP to the HubSpot deal and add DocuSign link once internal approvals are obtained.

I’ll update the MAP in Drive with the timelines and a short risk ladder. If everyone is available, I’ll run the internal alignment at 2pm PT tomorrow (link in Drive).

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Strategic GTM
Redwood Inference
